dct_title_s: Social Vulnerability Index (SVI) Overall Score by Census Tract, Massachusetts, 2020
dct_creator_sm: United States. Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry
Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (U.S.)
dct_description_sm: This layer consists of polygons representing Social Vulnerability Index (SVI) overall scores by 2020 Census Tracts for the state of Massachusetts. This dataset was derived and processed from the CDC ATSDR source dataset: SVI Interactive Map (https://www.atsdr.cdc.gov/place-health/php/svi/svi-interactive-map.html). This dataset contains only a small selection of the original attributes available in the source dataset and is joined with US Census Tract feature data downloaded from MassGIS. Please refer to the source data set to access the full set of data features. ATSDR's Geospatial Research, Analysis, & Services Program (GRASP) created the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry Social Vulnerability Index (CDC/ATSDR SVI or simply SVI, hereafter) to help public health officials and emergency response planners identify and map the communities that will most likely need support before, during, and after a hazardous event. SVI indicates the relative vulnerability of every U.S. Census tract. Census tracts are subdivisions of counties for which the Census collects statistical data. SVI ranks the tracts on 16 social factors, including unemployment, racial and ethnic minority status, and disability, and further groups them into four related themes. Thus, each tract receives a ranking for each Census variable and for each of the four themes as well as an overall ranking. For more information on SVI definitions and methodology please see: https://www.atsdr.cdc.gov/place-health/php/svi/svi-data-documentation-download.html
